topics.topic: Error contract for `store.read_records` when relation arguments are malformed (use of `internal_error` vs `unknown_reference`)
questions: Can `store.read_records` return `internal_error` for malformed relation arguments, or is `unknown_reference` its only non-success outcome?
For relation reads with wrong/missing argument kinds, is the required error always `internal_error`, and should this be part of the operation's formal error contract?

quotes:
A call that passes other arguments is a defect of its caller and
answers `internal_error` — so does one that omits an argument its relation
names or passes one of another kind; that defect is decided before any record
is looked up. The record a relation
names — every one of them — must exist, or the call is
`unknown_reference`, naming the first missing record in the order the
relation's name mentions them (A16 rule 1: checks in the order listed);
judgement.why: The text explicitly distinguishes malformed relation arguments (`internal_error`) from missing referenced records (`unknown_reference`).

topics.topic: Canonical JSON structure to hash for EffectAttempt idempotency keys with multiple fields
questions: What exact JSON structure is hashed when there are multiple key fields (object by field name, array in manifest order, or concatenated scalar tuple)?

topics.topic: How to derive TrialExecution execution class for masking when inputs are not explicitly named
questions: How must the kernel compute a TrialExecution's execution class (for masking `failure_detail` and value visibility) when TrialExecution does not name inputs?

topics.topic: Overall meaning/scope of `internal_error` across operations (write-only failure vs general internal fault including reads)
questions: Is `internal_error` strictly a failed-store-change condition, or a general sanitized internal failure code (including read-path faults)?

topics.topic: Representation used to measure JSON value size for `stored_value_bytes_max` and related bounds
questions: How is size measured for a JSON value when enforcing `stored_value_bytes_max`/other value bounds: canonical JSON UTF-8 bytes, original request bytes, or another representation?
Which set of services is iterated: all services in manifest, all services present in installation config, only services with selected instance, or only services with credentials?

questions: Is proof computation mandatory inside `compose_flow_version`, or only via a separate `prove_flow_version` call?

topics.topic: `list_records` behavior when a filter references a non-existent identity value
